canonical_claim: `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED FORGET` must publish terminal intent, trip the mount fence, stop renewal without clean release unless ref lanes are drained, stop GC, join keeper/remount/GC threads outside `remount_mutex`, and then enter `VanishedForgotten`.; FORGET is modeled in this order: mutex acquisition, idempotent `isVanished` short-circuit, intent publication, trip 1, GC stop and join, remount stop and join, trip 2, drain, `finishTeardown`, `keeperReset`, `enterVanished(Forgotten)`, and mutex release. [M1] prevents new remount attempts after intent publication, but an attempt that passed its bail may finish reclaim inside FORGET's join window; trip 2 closes that race.; The rev.7/rev.8 disk-lifecycle work landed a `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED FORGET` verb (with `GC STOP` / `GC START` companions) that unmounts a disk's pool by stopping all background CAS activity (GC, mount-lease renewal) and ejecting the disk, backed by a machine-checked (TLA+ Model 2) lifecycle state machine and an always-present `system.content_addressed_mounts`-style row per pool, rather than the previously-planned natural-erasure proof mechanism.
